answer.rationale: The incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, so renewal or renegotiation cannot meet the mandated 18% cost cut; deferring is risky because the contract does not auto-renew and the line has zero buffer at 94% committed volume, so a lapse would directly threaten delivery. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate outright, and memory_c2 (verified) indicates prior onboarding with a low-cost vendor was quick and invoicing stayed accurate, suggesting switching is operationally plausible. However, that memory is a single historical case from a different sourcing cycle and does not speak to performance under the current tight-capacity, no-buffer conditions, so I'm treating the switch as unproven at full scale. Rather than committing the entire primary volume immediately, I intend to initiate the switch as a guarded, limited-volume cutover alongside continuity safeguards, preserving the option to fall back if delivery reliability from the new vendor is not immediately confirmed. This keeps total cost of ownership in view (price plus risk of disruption) rather than optimizing price alone.
